diagnoses.summary: PCA indicates a strong SPE-driven, coherent upset with top contributors linked to CSTR holdup and tray temperatures, pointing to a restriction/outflow issue at the CSTR rather than a mere sensor fault. The strongest rule-based hypothesis is CSTR Outlet Capacity Loss, with secondary possibilities including CSTR Liquid Leak. Condenser cooling loss is plausible but less supported by the dominant SPE contributions at the CSTR and tray levels.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with simultaneous T2 and SPE violations. Saturated control loops around the CSTR outlet and risers suggest the disturbance originates in the CSTR outlet/feed handling, consistent with an outlet capacity issue driving holdup up and forcing compensatory actions.

The PCA shows a large, coherent plant upset with both T² and SPE violated, dominated by reactor holdup growth and high reactor/ CSTR outlet pressure signals, with cstr_holdup and cstr_outlet indicators as primary drivers. Several fixed-rule hypotheses point to CSTR outlet restrictions or leaks, with secondary contributions from condenser-related symptoms.

The PCA shows a large, coherent upset dominated by reactor holdup and related reactor variables, with multiple high/high-high alarms on the CSTR holdup loop. The strongest evidence points to loss of CSTR outlet capacity or a liquid leak causing unaccounted CSTR mass buildup and downstream disturbances. Sensor faults are less supported by the top contributors and alarms, while process faults on the CSTR side fit the observed pattern.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with strong SPE; several process indicators point to a disturbance propagating through the system. The rule-based hints favor a condenser/part of the CSTR feed and reactor performance faults, but the strongest catalogue-aligned candidate given the evidence is a catalyst activity/reaction-rate issue in the CSTR, with plausible contributing effects from condenser cooling and H2 vent actuation issues.

Abnormal PCA: large, coherent upset with strong acetone signals from CSTR outlet and bottoms, plus H2 vent and reflux controls active. High T2 and high SPE indicate a collective process deviation rather than a single sensor fault.

PCA indicates a large, coherent plant upset with significant deviations in multiple variables, dominated by H2 vent/PCV related signals. Rule-based hints point strongly to H2 PCV faults affecting reactor pressure control. Likely multiple PCV fault modes are active.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with multiple pressure-related measurements and controllers reacting; several actuator faults on the hydrogen PCV and recycle/reflux paths are plausible, with a sensor bias also possible. RB_LIC loop is saturated, suggesting a constraint or out-of-range control action contributing to the abnormal state. Bottoms acetone/pressure signals are also skewed, consistent with process disturbance propagating through the column and reactor outlets.

PCA flags a large, coherent process upset with reactor pressure and reboiler/column dynamics shifting together. The saturated RB_LIC loop indicates the reboiler level control is reaching its authority limit while plant pressures rise. Rule evidence supports a H2 PCV issue contributing to the pressure rise; multiple faults in the PCV domain are plausible if the PCV cannot open/respond as required.
High process upset with both T² and SPE violated; strongest evidence points to H2 PCV issues causing reactor pressure instability and downstream control saturation.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with both T² and SPE violated, with CSTR pressure and associated holdup signals driving the anomaly. Rule hints point to PCV-related issues (capacity or stuck valve) and a possible pressure sensor bias, compounded by a saturated RB_LIC loop. Most consistent with a sensor fault on reactor pressure (and potential PCV fault) causing incorrect readings and compensatory upsets.

A large, coherent plant upset with concurrent T² and SPE violations. The most likely cause is an actuator constraint/or saturation at the RB_LIC (reboiler loop), supported by downstream effects on reboiler holdup and column pressures, with plausible contributing faults in the H2 PCV and a biased reactor pressure sensor.

PCA shows a large, coherent plant upset with strong SPE; likely a liquid loss at the reboiler driving cascade effects and causing abnormal pressure/level signals. RB_LIC is saturated, supporting an abnormal outflow/level upset. Most consistent with a reboiler liquid leak driving the observed pattern (and possibly concurrent PCV/pressure sensing issues).

A large, coherent process upset with strong deviation in reboiler-related variables and reactor pressure suggests a fault in the hydrogen PCV (H2 PCV) system causing reduced venting capacity or stuck/ degraded valve behavior.

PCA shows a large coherent plant upset with both T² and SPE violated; strongest evidence points to a malfunction affecting pressure control and reboiler-related holdup, with possible PCV issues contributing to the abnormal correlations.
